Drizzle with coconut cream and salt

breakfast.name: Spam and Rice
instructions: Cook rice
Fry spam slices
Serve with soy sauce
breakfast.description: Pan-fried spam with rice — Pacific island staple.

breakfast.name: Spam and Rice Breakfast
instructions: Spam is a staple across the Pacific Islands — WWII American military presence embedded it
Palau was under US administration (UN Trust Territory) until 1994
Spam is not ironic here — it is genuine everyday protein, affordable and shelf-stable
Slice thick, fry in a dry pan until caramelized and crispy on both sides
Serve with hot sticky rice and a fried egg — the Pacific Island power breakfast
Soy sauce drizzled over everything — the Japanese influence on Palauan cuisine
This breakfast is shared across Micronesia, Hawaii, Guam — the Pacific Spam belt
breakfast.description: The Pacific Island power breakfast — Spam sliced thick and pan-fried until crispy-caramelized, served with sticky rice and a fried egg with soy sauce. WWII American military presence embedded Spam across the Pacific. Palau was a US-administered territory until 1994. Genuine everyday protein, shared across the Pacific Spam belt.

breakfast.name: Tapioca Porridge
instructions: Tapioca is one of Palau's traditional starch staples — from cassava root
Boil tapioca pearls in water until translucent
Add coconut milk and sugar — the porridge becomes creamy and sweet
Top with sliced ripe banana — tropical sweetness
This warming porridge is traditional breakfast in Palau's rural villages
Tapioca thrives in Palau's tropical volcanic soil
A gentle, sustaining breakfast before the heat of the day
breakfast.description: Palauan village breakfast — tapioca pearls boiled translucent, enriched with coconut milk and sugar, topped with sliced ripe banana. Tapioca (from cassava) thrives in Palau's tropical volcanic soil. Gentle and sustaining before the Pacific heat.

lunch.name: Tinola (Chicken Ginger Soup)
instructions: Sauté ginger and garlic
Add chicken, brown
Add water and green papaya
Simmer 20 min
Add chili leaves, season
lunch.description: Ginger chicken soup with green papaya.

lunch.name: Fruit Bat Soup
instructions: Clean fruit bat
Simmer in coconut milk with ginger, garlic
Add vegetables
Cook 45 min
lunch.description: Traditional Palauan delicacy — fruit bat in coconut milk.

lunch.name: Tinola (Palauan Chicken Soup)
instructions: Tinola is a clear ginger-chicken soup — shared across Micronesian and Filipino traditions
The Filipino community in Palau brought tinola; it merged with local cooking
Green papaya is the traditional vegetable — the unripe fruit cooks like a squash
The ginger base gives a warming, aromatic broth
Chicken simmered bone-in until tender — the bones give body to the broth
Add chili pepper leaves at the end — they wilt and add a mild peppery note
Seasoned with fish sauce — the umami base of Pacific Island cooking
lunch.description: Palauan ginger-chicken soup — bone-in chicken simmered with ginger, garlic, and green papaya (unripe, cooks like squash), finished with chili pepper leaves. Shared across Micronesian and Filipino traditions — Palau's Filipino community brought the dish and it merged with local cooking. The ginger broth is warming despite the tropical heat.

lunch.name: Ulkoy (Taro and Coconut Stew)
ingredients: Coconut milk (freshly squeezed from grated coconut)
instructions: Taro is Palau's most important traditional crop — cultivated for millennia
Palauan taro farming is women's knowledge — the taro patch (mesei) is women's domain
Peel and cube taro — it cooks into a starchy, slightly sticky texture
Simmer in coconut milk with fish or chicken until the taro softens
The coconut milk thickens as it reduces — creating a rich, creamy stew
Taro absorbs the coconut milk — becoming incredibly flavorful
This dish represents traditional Palauan cuisine before Western contact
lunch.description: Traditional Palauan stew — taro (Palau's staple, cultivated for millennia in women-managed mesei patches) simmered in freshly squeezed coconut milk with fish or chicken. The taro absorbs the rich coconut milk, becoming creamy and starchy. Represents pre-Western-contact Palauan cuisine. Taro farming is women's knowledge — the mesei is their domain.

lunch.name: Palauan Fish Soup
ingredients: Fresh reef fish (grouper, parrotfish — whatever is caught)
instructions: Palau is surrounded by some of the richest reef systems in the Pacific
Rock Islands Southern Lagoon is a UNESCO World Heritage site — extraordinary marine biodiversity
Fresh reef fish is the protein backbone of Palauan diet
Simmer fish in coconut milk with aromatics — the broth becomes rich and sweet
Add lemon or calamansi for acidity — it brightens the coconut richness
Taro leaves add green nutrition and earthy flavor
This simple soup is daily sustenance — fish + coconut milk + starch is the Palauan equation
lunch.description: Daily Palauan sustenance — fresh reef fish (from some of the Pacific's richest reef systems, UNESCO World Heritage) simmered in coconut milk with ginger, chili, and lemon juice. Fish + coconut milk + starch is the Palauan equation. Palau's Rock Islands Southern Lagoon has extraordinary marine biodiversity. The reef provides.

dinner.name: Grilled Parrotfish
instructions: Score fish, season with lime and salt
Grill until flaky
Serve with coconut cream

dinner.name: Pork and Taro in Coconut
instructions: Brown pork
Add taro and coconut milk
Simmer 35 min
dinner.description: Pork and taro in coconut milk.

dinner.name: Palauan Whole Roasted Fish
ingredients: Whole fish (red snapper or grouper — scored)
instructions: Roasting whole fish is one of Palau's oldest cooking traditions
Score the fish deeply — the seasonings and coconut cream penetrate the flesh
Stuff with ginger and garlic, coat in coconut cream
Wrap in banana leaves — the leaves steam the fish inside and impart green flavor
Roast over open fire or in an oven — the fish steams inside the leaf packet
The coconut cream becomes a sauce as the fish cooks
Whole fish preparation respects the catch — nothing is wasted
dinner.description: Palauan traditional roast — whole reef fish scored deeply, stuffed with ginger and garlic, coated in coconut cream, wrapped in banana leaves, and roasted until the fish steams inside the leaf packet. One of Palau's oldest cooking methods. The banana leaf imparts green flavor and the coconut cream becomes sauce. Respects the whole catch.

dinner.name: Ngiklel Temekai (Braised Mangrove Crab)
instructions: Mangrove crabs are plentiful in Palau's pristine mangrove ecosystems
The crabs are large, meaty, and prized — catching them is a skill
Clean and halve the crabs — simmer in coconut milk with aromatics
The coconut milk absorbs the crab flavor — becoming a rich, sweet-savory broth
Add chili for heat and lemon juice for brightness
Mangrove crab in coconut milk is festive — served at community gatherings (ocheraol)
Palau's mangrove forests are protected — sustainable harvesting is traditional practice
dinner.description: Palauan festive crab — mangrove crabs (from Palau's pristine ecosystems) simmered in coconut milk with garlic, ginger, and chili. Served at community gatherings (ocheraol). The coconut milk absorbs the crab sweetness. Mangrove forests are protected — sustainable harvesting is traditional practice in Palau.

dinner.name: Diokang (Pork and Taro)
instructions: Diokang is a traditional Palauan dish — pork and taro braised in coconut milk
Pork was introduced to Palau and became a ceremonial meat — used at customary events
Taro and pork together represent the land's bounty — root + protein + coconut
Simmer pork bone-in until tender, add taro and coconut milk
The taro softens and thickens the stew — the pork fat enriches the coconut broth
This dish appears at traditional Palauan ceremonies and community feasts
The combination is sustaining — designed to feed many at communal events
dinner.description: Traditional Palauan ceremonial dish — pork and taro braised in coconut milk until the taro thickens the stew and the pork fat enriches the broth. Pork is a ceremonial meat in Palau used at customary events. Root + protein + coconut = the land's bounty. Appears at community feasts designed to feed many.

snacks.name: Tapioca Balls
instructions: Mix tapioca with coconut cream and sugar
Shape into balls
Boil or steam 15 min

snacks.name: Fried Breadfruit
instructions: Breadfruit is one of Palau's traditional staple starches — alongside taro and cassava
The tree grows abundantly in Palau's tropical climate — a generous provider
Peel and slice breadfruit, fry in oil until golden and crispy
When ripe, breadfruit is slightly sweet — the frying caramelizes the sugars
Sprinkle with salt for savory or sugar for sweet
The texture: crispy outside, creamy-starchy inside — like a cross between potato and bread
Breadfruit was a critical food source across the Pacific — the Bounty mutiny was about breadfruit
snacks.description: Palauan staple snack — breadfruit (one of Palau's traditional starches) sliced and fried until golden and crispy-sweet. The tree grows abundantly in the tropical climate. Crispy outside, creamy-starchy inside — like a cross between potato and bread. The Bounty mutiny (1789) was about transporting breadfruit across the Pacific.

snacks.name: Cassava Cake
instructions: Cassava (tapioca plant) is a staple starch across the Pacific Islands
In Palau, grated fresh cassava is used for dense, chewy cakes
Mix grated cassava with coconut milk, sugar, eggs, butter, vanilla
Bake until set and golden on top — the texture is dense, chewy, slightly sticky
The coconut milk gives richness — the cassava gives chewiness
This cake is shared across Filipino, Chamorro, and Palauan traditions
Cassava must be properly prepared — peel thoroughly, the peel contains cyanogenic compounds
snacks.description: Pacific Island cassava cake — freshly grated cassava baked with coconut milk, sugar, and eggs into a dense, chewy, golden cake. Shared across Filipino, Chamorro, and Palauan traditions. The coconut milk gives richness, the cassava gives the distinctive chewy texture. Cassava must be peeled thoroughly — the peel contains cyanogenic compounds.

snacks.name: Green Banana Chips
instructions: Green (unripe) bananas are used as a starchy vegetable across the Pacific
Slice very thin — almost transparent — for maximum crispiness
Fry in hot oil until golden and crunchy — the starch crisps beautifully
Salt immediately while hot
In Palau, banana varieties include cooking bananas distinct from eating bananas
Green banana chips are a common snack sold at small stores and markets
The crunch is addictive — a tropical equivalent of potato chips
snacks.description: Palauan tropical chip — unripe green bananas sliced paper-thin and fried until golden and crunchy, salted immediately. Pacific Island cooking distinguishes between eating bananas and cooking bananas. The starch in unripe bananas crisps beautifully. A common snack at small stores and markets — the tropical potato chip.

desserts.name: Taro Cake
instructions: Mix taro with coconut cream and sugar
Pour into pan
Bake at 175°C 40 min
desserts.description: Dense, sweet taro cake with coconut.

desserts.name: Taro and Coconut Pudding
instructions: Taro is Palau's most important traditional food — this pudding celebrates it
Boil taro until very soft, mash until smooth
Mix with thick coconut cream and sugar — the combination is rich and starchy-sweet
The purple-gray color of taro gives the pudding a distinctive appearance
This is a traditional Palauan dessert — served at celebrations and feasts
Taro varieties in Palau number in the dozens — each with different flavor and texture
The women who cultivate taro are the knowledge keepers of Palau's food culture
desserts.description: Palauan celebration dessert — mashed taro (Palau's most important traditional crop) blended with thick coconut cream and sugar into a rich, starchy-sweet pudding with a distinctive purple-gray color. Served at feasts. Palau has dozens of taro varieties, each with different flavor. The women who cultivate taro are Palau's food culture knowledge keepers.

desserts.name: Banana in Coconut Milk
instructions: This simple dessert is found across the Pacific and Southeast Asia
Ripe bananas simmered gently in sweetened coconut milk until soft and caramelized
The salt enhances the sweetness — the combination is gentle and comforting
In Palau, this is a common after-meal dessert — easy, cheap, satisfying
The banana variety matters — Palauan cooking bananas hold their shape better
Served warm — the coconut milk thickens slightly as it cools
A dessert that represents the abundance of the tropical Pacific: banana + coconut = everywhere
desserts.description: Pacific simplicity — ripe bananas simmered in sweetened coconut milk until soft and gently caramelized. A common after-meal dessert in Palau — easy, cheap, deeply satisfying. A pinch of salt enhances the sweetness. Represents the tropical Pacific's abundance: banana + coconut are everywhere.

Drink fresh

Serve sweet or let ferment

drinks.name: Calamansi Juice (Palauan Style)
instructions: Calamansi grows throughout Palau — the small, fragrant citrus
Filipino and Southeast Asian influence brought calamansi cultivation to Palau
Squeeze many calamansi (they're small), mix with sugar and cold water
The flavor is more floral than regular lime — with mandarin-like overtones
Refreshing in Palau's tropical heat — often served at gatherings
Calamansi is used as both a drink and a seasoning in Palauan cooking
The small green fruit is a fixture in Palauan home gardens
drinks.description: Palauan refreshment — calamansi (small, fragrant citrus grown in Palauan home gardens, introduced through Filipino and Southeast Asian influence) squeezed and mixed with sugar and cold water. More floral than lime with mandarin overtones. Refreshing in the tropical Pacific heat. Used as both drink and cooking seasoning across Palau.
